note: Tutorial T00 lessons (spec §16): drive lessons on the Hinode Driving Grounds loop, judged from what the car does, each with a model demonstration and local retry; knowledge cards with one check question. Thresholds are design values for a first-time driver, checked against the demonstration runs; none is needed to start a race.

lessons.title: Controls and camera
lessons.goal: Drive to the 300 m board and change the camera view at least once on the way.
lessons.help: Throttle and brake are the triggers (W / S or the arrow keys), steering is the left stick (A / D). The camera button (C, or View on a pad) cycles close chase, far chase, hood, bumper and cockpit; hold look-back (B, or the right stick) to check behind. Settings keeps each view's comfort options.

lessons.title: Braking
lessons.goal: Arrive at the striped zone on the back straight above 70 km/h and shed at least 25 km/h inside it on the brake, without touching a wall.
lessons.help: Brake in a straight line first and hardest at the start; ease off as the car slows so the front tyres can steer again (trail braking). Braking late but too hard only moves the problem into the corner.

lessons.title: Turn-in and exits
lessons.goal: Take the Demonstration Bend without touching a wall and leave it above 40 km/h.
lessons.help: Turn in once, smoothly, when the car is settled; aim to be on the throttle as the bend opens. A slow, tidy entry gives a faster exit — exit speed is carried all the way down the next straight.

lessons.title: Grip versus drift
lessons.goal: Score a drift in the Demonstration Bend's judged zone (at least 300 raw points).
lessons.help: Grip is the faster way round most corners; drifting is scored only in judged zones. Unsettle the rear with a flick or the handbrake (Space, or A on a pad) at speed, hold the angle with the throttle and catch it with opposite lock. Walls, spins and leaving the road lose the unbanked chain.

lessons.title: Countersteering
lessons.goal: Catch a slide: let the car slip past 12 degrees and bring it back straight without spinning or touching a wall.
lessons.help: When the rear steps out, steer the way it is going (opposite lock) and ease the throttle; unwind the lock as the car straightens so it does not snap the other way.

lessons.title: Exits and gearing
lessons.goal: Run the timed straight from the acceleration board to the end board in under 20 seconds.
lessons.help: A clean exit onto a straight is worth more than a late brake before it. With manual gears (E / Q, or the bumpers), shift up near the top of the rev bar and keep the engine in its band; automatic does this for you.

lessons.title: Resets and checkpoints
lessons.goal: Hold reset once, then drive on 100 m from where it puts you.
lessons.help: Holding reset (R, or Y on a pad) for under a second returns the car to the last safe checkpoint behind it, adds 3.0 s and clears any drift chain; the car is briefly ghosted. It never moves you forward or skips a checkpoint. A car stuck or on its roof is offered recovery.

lessons.title: Ghost deltas
lessons.goal: Finish a lap with the instructor's demonstration ghost on the road and read the checkpoint deltas.
lessons.help: A ghost is a recorded run, not a car: it cannot touch you and occupies no grid slot. At each checkpoint the HUD shows how far ahead (−) or behind (+) you are; after the race the route chart shows where the time went.

lessons.title: Parts and stats
lessons.goal: Compare a part before you buy it.
lessons.help: The Garage shows each part's effect on the car's stats and on its PI (performance index) before you buy; classes cap PI. The car you race is the build frozen when the event starts.
lessons.question: Which build races in an event?
choices: Whatever you change in the Garage during the race
The build frozen when the event starts
lessons.explanation: The build is frozen at the start, so nobody can change a car mid-event.

lessons.title: Raw versus showcase score
lessons.help: Drift events rank by the raw score the server judged in the zones. A showcase number on your card is presentation — it never changes a result.
lessons.question: Which score ranks a drift event?
choices: The raw score judged in the zones
The showcase number on your card
lessons.explanation: Only the judged raw score ranks; the showcase is for display.

lessons.title: Convoy readiness
lessons.goal: Know how a convoy starts an event.
lessons.help: The leader proposes a mode; everyone marks Mode Ready; the leader enters it and proposes an event; everyone marks Event Ready; then the leader starts. Your car and build are checked when you mark ready. A practice ready-check never needs a stranger.
lessons.question: Who must be Event Ready before the leader can start?
lessons.explanation: Every racing member marks Event Ready; spectators do not.

lessons.title: Public meets
lessons.goal: Know what a meet is for.
lessons.help: The car meet is a social space: walk, park your car on display, chat and use the interaction spots. Nothing in a meet is ever required for rank, and you can leave at any time.
lessons.question: Does anything at a public meet decide your rank?
choices: Yes, the time you spend there
lessons.explanation: Meets are social; rank comes from sanctioned events and challenges.

lessons.title: Race connectivity and disqualification
lessons.goal: Know what happens if you drop out.
lessons.help: Online races run on a server. If you disconnect you may rejoin your convoy; your entry in the race already running stays disqualified, but you can spectate it. Leaving after your accepted finish keeps your result.
lessons.question: You disconnect mid-race and rejoin the convoy. What about that race?
choices: Your entry stays disqualified, but you can spectate
lessons.explanation: A left race stays a disqualification; spectating is offered.

lessons.title: Rewards and rank
lessons.goal: Know where credits and rank come from.
lessons.help: Credits come from finishing events (more for placing and clean driving), first clears and challenges; rank points come from clears and challenges. Offline (Local) progress stays on this PC and never becomes online currency.
lessons.question: Can offline progress be moved into your online wallet?
choices: No — Local and Online stay separate
lessons.explanation: Local progress never becomes online currency, unlocks, rank or records.
